title: Accounts Administration Assistant
description:
12-Month Fixed-Term Contract

A fantastic opportunity has arisen to join the finance shared services team of a highly successful global organisation operating within a fast-paced, technology-led environment.

This 12-month fixed-term position has been created to support the continued growth of the European Shared Service Centre and offers the chance to become part of a collaborative finance team supporting multiple international business entities.

The Role

As a Travel & Expense (T&E) Administrator, you will be responsible for ensuring the accurate and timely audit of employee travel and expense claims, providing support with payment activities, and delivering excellent customer service to stakeholders across the business.

Working within a dedicated team, you will help maintain compliance with company policies, resolve employee queries and contribute to the smooth operation of the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Auditing travel and expense submissions in line with company policies and internal controls
- Reviewing and resolving employee and stakeholder queries relating to expenses and financial transactions
- Supporting regular payment runs across multiple entities
- Assisting with month-end and year-end finance processes
- Supporting the preparation of financial reports and documentation
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner
- Maintaining employee data in accordance with data protection requirements
- Working closely with colleagues and other departments to support efficient financial operations
- Contributing to process improvements, training and knowledge-sharing activities
- Supporting wider shared service centre activities as required
- Occasional travel to support finance projects and system implementations

Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will ideally possess:
- Previous experience within a transactional finance environment
- Experience using a Travel & Expense platform such as Concur, Chrome River or SAP
- ERP system experience, with SAP highly desirable
- Strong Microsoft Excel and Office skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Effective communication and stakeholder management abilities
- A proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills
- The ability to work independently and collaboratively
- A positive, customer-focused mindset

Qualifications
- Prior experience in finance administration, accounts payable or transactional finance preferred
- AAT studies or qualification would be advantageous but are not essential

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Annual bonus opportunity
- Flexible and hybrid working arrangements
- Exposure to a global finance function within a growing international organisation
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to contribute to ongoing finance transformation projects

Location

This is a hybrid position based in South Wales. Following an initial training period of approximately 12 weeks, the role will operate on a 3 days office / 2 days home working basis.

title: Contract Support Associate
description:
Company Profile

CBRE is the global leader in commercial real estate services and investment. We help our clients and communities realise their potential through industry-leading expertise, innovation, and integrated solutions.

Job Title: Contract Support Associate

As a CBRE Contract Support Associate, you will provide exceptional customer service and administrative support to a large Business Unit, Facility, or Account.

Role Summary:
- This role is part of the Contract Quality Management job function and is responsible for supporting the delivery of contractual services to ensure requirements are fulfilled.
- Respond to client inquiries and concerns and ensure timely and quality service delivery and follow-up to ensure satisfaction.
- Understand the scope of the contract and make sure that all work is carried out accordingly.
- Be a financial and operational systems champion. Suggest efforts to put in place cost-saving opportunities to maximise customer and financial savings targets.
- Coordinate and onboard vendors for reactive and planned works and manage subcontractor paperwork.
- Review processed invoices and ensure accurate cost centre coding. Coordinate the billing application, calculate margins, raise invoices, and submit to clients. Work closely with site teams and head office, ensuring accurate processing of quotations and purchase orders.
- Review and approve maintenance billing invoices and projects as per contracted agreements. Ensure consistent delivery of core operational and financial outputs on the account.
- Respond to inquiries on financial reports for Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, and open purchase orders.
- Deliver monthly reporting support on Contract and Business Unit Reviews.
- Assist in ensuring compliance with Health & Safety requirements, including HSE reporting and promoting a safe work environment. Maintain QHSE documentation and ensure it is available using company systems.
- Gather and analyse data to identify and solve complex problems that arise with little or no precedent. May recommend new techniques.
- Impact own team and other teams whose work activities are closely related.
- Suggest improvements to existing processes and solutions to improve the efficiency of the team.

Experience Required:
- A comprehensive understanding of a range of processes, procedures, systems, and concepts within own job function.
- Ability to evaluate and communicate unusual and/or complex content in a concise and logical way.
- In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.
- Strong organisational skills with an advanced inquisitive mindset.
- Advanced mathematical skills with the ability to calculate percentages, discounts, and mark-ups.

DISCLAIMER

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this role. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to the job. CBRE reserves the right to modify this job description at any time without notice.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Location: Newport

Salary: £27,810 per annum

Hours: 40 hours per week

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Working Arrangement: Fully office-based

The Opportunity

Môrwell Talent Solutions is working with an established organisation to recruit an organised, efficient and proactive Accounts Assistant to join their finance team.

This is a varied, hands-on role combining day-to-day accounts responsibilities with general administrative duties. We are looking for someone who takes pride in keeping things organised, works methodically and accurately, and is confident taking ownership of their workload.

The successful candidate will enjoy variety, be comfortable managing competing priorities and be happy getting involved wherever needed to support the smooth running of the department. Strong communication skills are essential, particularly the confidence to pick up the phone, speak with colleagues, suppliers and customers, and proactively follow up on outstanding queries.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous accounts experience who enjoys working in a busy team and is looking for a varied role where they can contribute to the wider business.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts & Finance
- Process supplier invoices and assist with purchase ledger administration, payments and supplier account reconciliations.
- Support sales ledger activities, including raising invoices, monitoring outstanding balances and chasing overdue payments.
- Complete bank reconciliations and reconcile payments received through various channels.
- Assist with daily income reconciliations, ensuring financial records are accurate and up to date.
- Investigate discrepancies, resolve queries and liaise with relevant departments, suppliers and customers.
- Support month-end activities, financial reporting and other accounts duties as required.

Administration & Communication
- Provide general administrative support to the finance department and wider business.
- Maintain accurate records, spreadsheets, filing systems and financial documentation.
- Respond to telephone calls and emails from colleagues, suppliers and customers in a professional and timely manner.
- Confidently pick up the phone to chase information, resolve queries and follow up on outstanding issues.
- Liaise with other departments to ensure information is communicated effectively and tasks are completed promptly.
- Manage competing priorities, use initiative and ensure actions are followed through to completion.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who is highly organised, methodical and proactive, with a keen eye for detail and the ability to manage their workload efficiently.

You will be a confident communicator who is comfortable speaking to people at all levels, happy to undertake both accounts and administrative duties, and willing to take ownership rather than waiting to be told what needs doing.

Essential skills and experience:
- Previous experience in an accounts or finance environment.
- An understanding of purchase ledger and sales ledger processes.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Strong organisational, numerical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including confidence using the telephone.
- A professional approach to accuracy, confidentiality and teamwork.
- The ability to work independently, prioritise tasks and use initiative.

Experience within a hotel, hospitality or similar multi-department environment would be advantageous, as would familiarity with accounting software or property management systems.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £27,810 per annum.
- 20 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Statutory pension scheme.
- Life assurance scheme.
- The opportunity to join an established finance team in a varied role combining accounts, administration and communication.

Interested?

If you are an organised, efficient and proactive individual who enjoys a varied role, takes pride in getting things done and is confident picking up the phone, we would love to hear from you.

Please contact Môrwell Talent Solutions for further information or to discuss the opportunity in confidence.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Temporary Bookkeeper

Location: Newport

Pay Rate: £15.80-£16.15 per hour + holiday pay

Hours: Full-time (37.5 hours per week) or part-time (32 hours per week)

Contract: Temporary, with the potential to become permanent

Start Date: Immediate

The Opportunity

Môrwell Talent Solutions is currently recruiting for a Temporary Bookkeeper to join a business based in Newport, providing cover for a period of on-going sickness. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional to join the business at short notice and support the day-to-day running of the finance function.

Reporting directly to the Operations Manager, you will be responsible for a varied range of bookkeeping and finance administration duties, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient operation of the department. The role would ideally suit an AAT-qualified or QBE finance professional. There may also be the potential for the position to become permanent for the right candidate.

Key Responsibilities will include -
- Managing the purchase ledger, including processing supplier invoices and maintaining accurate records.
- Managing the sales ledger, ensuring invoices are raised and accounts are kept up to date.
- Carrying out credit control duties, including monitoring outstanding payments and following up on overdue accounts.
- Performing regular bank and account reconciliations.
- Maintaining accurate financial records using Xero.
- Providing general finance administration support to the Operations Manager and wider business.
- Assisting with day-to-day bookkeeping tasks and ensuring financial information is accurate and up to date.

About You
- Previous experience in a bookkeeping or finance role is essential.
- Relevant experience using Xero is essential.
- Ideally AAT-qualified or Qualified by Experience.
- A good understanding of purchase ledger, sales ledger, credit control and reconciliations.
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to work.
- Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage a varied workload.
- A reliable, proactive approach and the ability to work independently when required.
- Available to start immediately or at very short notice.

Working Arrangements

The role will initially be fully office-based in Newport, with the possibility of some hybrid working further down the line, depending on business needs.

The client is happy to consider candidates seeking either 37.5 hours per week or 32 hours per week, offering some flexibility around working hours.

What's on Offer?
- £15.80-£16.15 per hour, plus holiday pay.
- Immediate start on offer.
- A varied bookkeeping role within an established business.
- Potential for the position to become permanent.
- Consideration for both full-time and part-time working arrangements.

Interested?

If you have relevant bookkeeping experience, are confident using Xero and are available to start at short notice, we'd love to hear from you. Please contact Môrwell Talent Solutions to find out more or apply for the role.

title: Personal Assistant
description:
Yolk Recruitment is pleased to be supporting a values-led community housing organisation, with a strong focus on people, communities and delivering excellent services to customers, in the appointment of an experienced Personal Assistant to provide high-quality support to an Executive Director and members of the Senior Leadership Group.

The opportunity

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced PA who enjoys working in a fast-paced, senior environment and takes pride in being the person who keeps things organised, moving and on track.

You'll be a trusted and proactive partner to senior leaders, helping them manage competing priorities and ensuring they are well supported to deliver their strategic objectives.

You'll join an established team of three PAs, working collaboratively and providing cover for one another as required. You'll need to be confident working independently, but equally comfortable as part of a close-knit team.

With the role starting in December 2026, we're ideally looking for someone who can hit the ground running and bring strong PA experience from day one.

What you'll be doing

You'll provide a high-quality PA service to senior leaders, including:
- Managing complex diaries and multiple calendars, ensuring priorities are effectively coordinated.
- Managing busy inboxes, prioritising correspondence and ensuring actions are followed through.
- Acting as a trusted gatekeeper, using sound judgement when managing requests and escalating issues where appropriate.
- Coordinating meetings from start to finish, including agendas, papers, logistics, minutes and follow-up actions.
- Preparing reports, presentations, briefing papers and other documentation.
- Supporting travel, accommodation and event arrangements.
- Building strong relationships with colleagues, external partners and stakeholders.
- Handling confidential and sensitive information with absolute discretion.
- Maintaining effective digital filing and document management systems, including SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Supporting recruitment and people-related processes associated with senior roles.
- Working flexibly across the PA team, providing cover and support to colleagues when required.
- Anticipating the needs of senior leaders and proactively resolving issues before they arise.
- Supporting meetings and activities across the organisation, including travel where required.

What we're looking for

We're looking for an experienced PA who is highly organised, proactive and adaptable, with the confidence to work with senior leaders and manage competing demands.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience working as a PA or in a similar executive support role within a professional office environment.
- Experience supporting senior managers, executives or leadership teams.
- Strong diary and inbox management experience.
- Experience coordinating meetings, including preparing agendas and papers, minute taking and tracking actions through to completion.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Experience building effective relationships with colleagues, senior stakeholders and external contacts.
- Experience handling confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work to deadlines.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office applications and digital systems.
- An understanding of confidentiality, data protection, cyber security and information governance principles.
- The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player.

It would be great if you also have:
- Experience using digital office systems such as One Advanced.
- Experience with SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Experience arranging travel, accommodation and events.
- Experience working within a housing, public sector, not-for-profit or similarly structured organisation.

Benefits
- Four-day working week pilot - currently extended until the end of October 2026, before a decision is made on whether to extend or make the arrangement permanent.
- 23 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays
- 12% employer contribution to the Social Housing Pension Scheme from day one
- Investment in learning and development
- Health cash plan
- 24/7 mental health support
- 24/7 online GP service
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay
- Employee discount platform
- Occupational Health service
- Free parking

To apply

Please submit your up-to-date CV detailing how you meet the criteria of the role, to Hannah Welfoot at Yolk Recruitment.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Office Administrator Accounts Administrator Payroll Administrator

Newport Well-Established Roofing Company Office-Based Role

Working hours:

Monday to Thursday 09:00am - 16:30pm

Friday 09:00am - 16:00pm

1 hour paid lunch every day

Salary will be based of experience and capabilities

Introduction

Acorn by Synergie is recruiting an experienced Office Administrator to join a well-established roofing company based in Newport.

This is a varied position that combines administration, accounts, payroll, HR support and customer communication. As the central point of the office, you will play an important role in maintaining accurate financial records, supporting business operations and ensuring professional communication with clients, suppliers and colleagues.

What We Offer
- A supportive team environment where your contributions are valued.
- Modern office facilities with all the tools you need to succeed.
- The opportunity to make a direct impact on the smooth running and growth of the business.

Key Duties / Key Responsibilities
- Manage Sage Accounts, including sales ledger and purchase ledger entries.
- Complete bank reconciliations and online banking runs (BACS).
- Carry out credit control and VAT return activities.
- Produce monthly statements and maintain file retention records for monies due.
- Prepare end-of-year accounts for the Accountant.
- Oversee Sage Payroll processes.
- Process weekly payroll and submit information via the Government Gateway portal.
- Complete weekly pension assessments and submissions via the pension portal.
- Prepare year-end PAYE documentation.
- Maintain stationery supplies and office resources.
- Organise and manage filing systems and document retention processes.
- Support HR administration and accurate record-keeping.
- Type quotations, tenders, priced bills, invoices and letters.
- Answer telephone calls and manage incoming and outgoing emails.
- Ensure all correspondence is clear, accurate and timely.
- Support business operations through efficient data entry and keyboard skills.

Requirements

Essential Requirements
- Proven experience using Sage Accounts and Sage Payroll.
- Strong understanding of sales ledger, purchase ledger, bank reconciliations, VAT returns and credit control.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines.
